paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 187 of 2006
State of Uttaranchal ............. Revisionist
 versus
Ibraj ............. Respondent
Mr. P.S. Saun, AGA for the revisionist State.
Mr. Amish Tiwari, Advocate for the respondent.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J. (oral)

A criminal revision was preferred by the
State of Uttarakhand against the impugned order dated
19.05.2006, passed by learned Addl. Sessions Judge /
4th FTC, Haridwar, in criminal revision no. 211 of
2005, Ibraj vs State of Uttaranchal, whereby the order
dated 01.06.2005, passed by learned Civil Judge (Junior
Division) / Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee was set aside.
Learned Magistrate vide order dated 01.06.2005
summoned the accused persons to face the trial in
respect of offences punishable under Section 323, 504,
506 and 452 of IPC.
2) Accused Ibraj s/o Latur r/o Village
Balawali, police station Khanpur, Tehsil Laksar,
District Haridwar was to stand trial before learned
Magistrate, Roorkee in connection with case no. 225 of
2004, captioned as Babu Ram vs Ved Pal and others,
relating to police station Khanpur, District Haridwar
under Sections 323, 504, 506 and 452 of IPC.

2
3) An application was presented before the
learned Magistrate on behalf of the accused-respondent
Ibraj that since the accused has been falsely implicated
in the case due to enmity, therefore, he should be
acquitted, in as much as there was no sufficient
evidence against him. Learned Magistrate, vide order
dated 01.06.2005 held, on the basis of statements of
injured and the witness (PW2 Rishipal) under Section
245 of Cr.P.C., that a prima facie case was made out
against the accused. Aggrieved against said order dated
01.06.2005, accused preferred criminal revision no. 211
of 2005, captioned as Ibraj vs State of Uttaranchal. The
revision court, vide order dated 19.05.2006, allowed the
criminal revision and set aside the order dated
01.06.2005.
4) Aggrieved against said order, present
criminal revision was preferred by the State of
Uttarakhand, and not on behalf of the complainant
Babu Ram. It may be noted here that Babu Ram
alongwith State of Uttarakhand was heard when the
criminal revision was decided by learned Addl.
Sessions Judge / 4th FTC, Haridwar. In a complaint
case, Babu Ram was the affected party, who did not file
criminal revision against the impugned order dated
19.05.2006.
5) Learned counsel for the respondent
submitted that a third person like State of Uttarakhand

3
cannot challenge the impugned order, in as much as it
was a private criminal complaint case between Babu
Ram and Ibraj. State of Uttarakhand had no right to
participate in the proceedings of the complaint case
before the learned Magistrate. If an alien to a
proceeding does not have any right to participate in any
proceeding, he also does not possess the right to
challenge any order passed in the said proceeding. The
law does not confer such right on anybody. The
criminal revision on behalf of an alien was not
maintainable and was also barred by Section 397(2) of
Cr.P.C. Learned counsel for the respondent relied upon
the ruling of Dr. Harvir Singh vs State of U.P. and
another, 2007 Indian Law Reports Allahabad Series
486. Paras no. 10 and 11 of said ruling are being
reproduced here-in-under for ready reference:
"10. Further in the present case the lower revisional
 court, without caring to look in to the various
 rulings cited by it in the impugned order has
 allowed the revision filed by an alien to a
 proceeding. How the revision by an alien to the
 proceeding was maintainable before the lower
 revisional court against the statutory bar provided
 under Section 397 (2) CR.P.C. is not
 understandable. The lower revisional court did
 not address itself at all to the statutory provision
 under Section 397(2) Cr.P.C. and cogitated on the
 fact that the order passed by the Judicial
 Magistrate Court No. 3 Aligarh dated 17.11.2006,

4
 which as impugned before it, was purely an
 interlocutory order and no revision against the said
 order was maintainable before it being barred by
 section 397(2) Cr.P.C. The Additional Sessions
 Judge, Court No. 11, Aligarh Sri N.A. Zaidi,
 therefore, passed a wholly illegal order by
 usurping the power of the revisional court under
 Section 397(2) Cr.P.C. Such type of interference
 by the lower revisional court in the proceedings
 pending before the Magistrates not only delays the
 trial but creates utter confusion, saddling the
 Magistrates with unmanageable load of work
 which must be curbed. Section 397(2) Cr.P.C. has
 been ingrafted in the Statute (Code) for being
 observed and not to be ignored. No revision
 against an interlocutory order, therefore, was
 maintainable before the lower revisional Court,
 specially when it was conceded before me that the
 order passed by the Magistrate, which was
 challenged in revision before the lower revisional
 court was pure and simple interlocutory order at
 the stage of an inquiry under Section 202 Cr.P.C.
 Thus the impugned order passed by the Additional
 Sessions Judge, Court No. 11, Aligarh in criminal
 revision no. 541 of 2006 dated 22.1.2007 is
 wholly an illegal order and cannot be sustained at
 all.
11. There is yet another bizarre aspect of the matter
 and that is how a third person can challenge an
 order passed by a Magistrate when he has no right

5
 to participate in the proceedings. If an alien to a
 proceeding does not have any right to participate
 in any proceeding, he also does not possess the
 right to challenge any order passed in the said
 proceeding. The law does not confer any such
 right on any body. R.K. Savita, respondent no. 2,
 being an alien to the proceeding had no right to
 maintain the revision before the lower revisional
 court, which was wrongly entertained by it and
 has been illegally allowed."
6) A private criminal complaint case was filed
by Babu Ram against Ibraj, in which Ibraj was
summoned to face the trial for the offences punishable
under Sections 323, 504, 506, 452 of IPC. Thereafter,
two witnesses were examined under Section 244 of
Cr.P.C. on behalf of complainant Babu Ram. On the
basis of such evidence, learned Magistrate, having
found a prima facie case against the accused, directed
that the charge in respect of said offences shall be
framed against the accused Ibraj. Aggrieved against
said order, Ibraj preferred criminal revision in which
State of Uttarakhand was arrayed as respondent no. 1
and Babu Ram was arrayed as respondent no. 2. After
hearing the submissions of both the sides, the criminal
revision preferred on behalf of Ibraj was allowed and
the order dated 01.06.2005, passed by learned
Magistrate was set aside. State of Uttarakhand was
only a formal party in the said revision. State of

6
Uttarakhand was not a party in a private criminal
complaint case filed by Babu Ram against Ibraj in the
Court of Magistrate. In such a situation, this Court is
inclined to accept the argument of learned counsel for
the respondent that State of Uttarakhand had no locus to
file the present criminal revision.
7) The criminal revision filed on behalf of the
State of Uttarakhand is accordingly disposed of as not
maintainable. This is without prejudice to the rights
of the complainant / injured to challenge the
impugned order by way of filing criminal revision.
